name: OH-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+10 district lean favors incumbent David Joyce
Joyce holds a massive financial edge ($3.1M vs $34K cash)
No polls or expert ratings; markets price ~96% Republican
Joyce is a well-established incumbent seeking renomination and reelection
model.rationale: The forecast rests on the district's R+10 lean, Joyce's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage, with prediction markets pricing a Republican win near 96%. No polls or expert ratings justify moving materially from the fundamentals-based estimate of roughly R+14.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Joyce under 55% or a surge of outside spending against him would be the first sign of a real race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican David Joyce seeks another term in a northeastern Ohio district that leans about ten points Republican at the presidential level. He is a well-funded incumbent with more than $3.1 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Maria Jukic has raised only about $62,000 and has minimal cash available. No outside groups are spending against Joyce, and no independent polls of the race are available.

Prediction markets put Joyce's chances near 96 percent, and no expert raters list the seat as competitive. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican win in the mid-teens, with modest residual uncertainty because polling is absent. A major environmental shift or unexpected candidate development would be needed to put this seat in play.
